items.note: It takes on the price question head-on. Pro at $69 churned 10 of 12, against 1 of 8 at $49, and all of those cancels fall in Aug–Sep. It says honestly that the file has no price history or cancel reasons, so it can't prove the price caused the churn. I re-checked the counts against the data and they are correct.
It removes the 15 trial accounts and lists them by ID. All later figures use the cleaned set of 40 accounts.
It removes the 5 @ourco.test accounts (IDs 1056–1060) and explains how they would have inflated August churn and the $69 rate.
It counts churn as any account with a cancel_month, and says these are cumulative rates.

It isn't written for a CEO. It opens with a note about hand counting and pandas, then runs through many tables, cohort breakdowns and data-engineering open questions. There is no short executive framing.
It isn't a summary of at most 5 bullets. It has several sections, multiple tables and well over 5 bullets.
It never suggests a chart or says what to plot.

It flags small samples throughout: Pro $49 has n=8, each cohort has n=8, and some months have only one cancel. It also says price as the cause is only a hypothesis the data can't confirm. However, it never gives one overall confidence rating.
